front: Sources of the raw materials for the Haber process
back: Nitrogen: air (fractional distillation of liquid air). Hydrogen: methane + steam, or electrolysis of water.

front: Why about 450 °C in the Haber process?
back: Lower temperature gives more ammonia (exothermic) but is too slow; 450 °C is a compromise.

front: Why about 200 atm in the Haber process?
back: 4 → 2 gas molecules, so high pressure raises yield and rate; higher pressures cost too much and are more dangerous.

front: Role of iron in the Haber process
back: Increases the rate (equilibrium reached faster); does not change the yield.

front: How is ammonia removed from the converter gases?
back: Cooling: ammonia (b.p. −33 °C) liquefies; N₂ and H₂ stay as gases.

front: Why recycle unreacted N₂ and H₂?
back: Only about 15% reacts per pass; recycling converts almost all of it eventually.
